newsitem.title: UK: Telefonica to pay up for data network - Unisource.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica to pay up for data network - Unisource.

text.p: Ben Verwaayen, the chairman of AT&T Unisource, warned Telefonica de Espana SA on Friday that the flagship Spanish carrier would have to pay up if it abandoned its international alliance.
"Unisource owns the data network in Spain -- not Telefonica anymore. We certainly will not give it (away) for free," Verwaayen told CNBC Europe television.

Telefonica said earlier it was initiating steps to withdraw from Unisource, after announcing it had formed a strategic alliance with Unisource's arch-rival Concert, a partnership between British Telecommunications Plc and America's MCI Communications Corp.

Verwaayen, who is also the president of Unisource member PTT Telecom of the Netherlands, accused Telefonica's new management of violating contracts that they were "so anxious to go into" less than a year ago.
"The first thing we will do is file with them our position. We ask them to leave immediately," he said, adding that they groups would try to settle outstanding issues "in clear negotiations".
He said there had hardly been any integration of Telefonica in the Unisource alliance, which is led by U.S. telecoms giant AT&T Corp and includes Telia of Sweden and Swiss Telecom PTT.
But he denied that a defection of Telefonica would be a major setback for the rival alliance, adding that the group would be "extremely careful" in selecting any new partners.
"This is an alliance between Europe and the United States and combined, we have the necessary power to serve the market in the best (possible way)," he said.

Analysts have speculed that Italian telecoms holding company STET(Societa Finanziaria Telefonica per Azioni Spa) may fill Telefonica's seat. STET remains one of the few, major, European telecoms operators that remain unattached.
